safe-place.text: An agent that runs commands needs somewhere safe to do it. OpenClaw runs in its own container, and the Hub's authenticated proxy sits in front of its gateway.

open.text: This is OpenClaw, set up for Companion Hub.

first-run.text: First run is a setup page. Add your provider keys there. There is no interactive onboarding command, and the gateway token is managed for you.

chat.text: Then it opens on a chat, ready to go, with a few starter prompts to try.

toolbox.text: Inside the sandbox it has Python, Node, Homebrew and a headless browser. What it installs under its data folder persists across app updates.

memory.text: Give it a Companion Memory address and key, and its memory moves there. Each finished turn is saved. The Hub's own wake-up messages are left out, so memory never files them as you.

approval.text: It can list Companion's intents and run them by name. Destructive or external ones are queued as an approval card for the owner.

boundary.text: One rule. Keep the gateway on a private network or behind the Hub's proxy. A container alone does not make an agent safe to expose.

close.text: OpenClaw, from Companion Intelligence. UnCloud your life.
